settings.title: Settings
settings.ltcOutputHelp: Where this show sends SMPTE timecode. It is a name, not a sound card — this machine's output map decides what it means here.
settings.ltcOutputUnavailableHelp: “{name}” is not mapped here and names no device on this machine, so timecode is silent. Map it under Hardware Outputs, or choose another.
settings.outputTargetHelp: Sets the brickwall limiter level, meter zone colours, waveform colours, and auto-volume target for this project.
settings.meterModeHelp: Unit shown on all stereo meters.
settings.meterBallisticsHelp: How fast the meters rise and fall.
settings.disableAutoVolumeAndTrim: Disable automatic volume and trim adjustments
settings.disableLimiterHelp: Turns off the brickwall limiter, allowing peaks above the output ceiling. Can be changed during playback.
settings.disableSilenceWarningHelp: Stops the silence warning banner from appearing in the header.
settings.transitionModeHelp: Transition applied to newly imported tracks. Each track can still be switched between cross-fade and start-next in its properties.
settings.autoCueNext: Automatically cue next item even without end behaviour
settings.autoCueNextHelp: Arms the next item as "Up Next" even when the playing item has no end behaviour, so you can step through the playlist with a single GO button. It does not start playback automatically.
settings.stopAllFadeHelp: How long all cues take to fade out when you press Stop All. Set to 0 for an instant stop.
settings.scrollToPlayingHelp: Automatically keep the currently-playing item centred in the list.
settings.indexDisplayStartHelp: Controls the number shown for the first playlist item. Internal indexes and API index paths remain zero-based.
settings.routingInMixer: Audio routing lives in the mixer. Each cue plays through a bus; each bus sends to a hardware output, another bus, or the Preview bus for headphones.
settings.sectionPlaybackHelp: How cues start, end and hand over to one another. These travel with the show.
settings.sectionAudioHelp: Output level standard, limiting, metering and timecode for this show.
settings.sectionMixerHelp: How the mixer is laid out on this screen. Remembered on this machine, not in the show and not in your account — a console display and a laptop want different answers.
settings.mixerViewHelp: Choosing a docked view opens the mixer if it is closed. The panel’s own Dock and Expand buttons change this too.
settings.mixerViewNoWindow: A separate window needs the desktop app. In a browser the mixer can only be docked or fill the workspace.
settings.sectionKeyboardHelp: Keys for transport actions and cart slots. Click a row, then press the combination you want.
settings.sectionSurfacesHelp: MIDI controllers. Arm Learn on an action, then move the control you want to bind to it.
settings.sectionProjectHelp: How this project saves itself and numbers its cues.
settings.autosaveHelp: Saves the project after every edit. When off, the project is only written by File > Save and an "Unsaved Changes" pill appears beside the title.
settings.sectionServerHelp: Which server this app talks to, and — for an administrator — what that server does.
settings.sectionUsersHelp: Who may use this server, and what they are allowed to change.
settings.stopAllStopsPreview: Stop All also stops the preview
settings.stopAllStopsPreviewHelp: When off, Stop All leaves a cue you are pre-listening to on the preview bus playing.
settings.sectionAppearanceHelp: How LivePlay looks and reads on this screen. These are yours, not the show’s — they follow you rather than the file.
settings.languageHelp: Yours alone, and only on this screen — it does not change what anyone else connected to this show sees.
settings.themeModeHelp: Dark is the default: a lit screen in a dark control room is the usual case.
settings.themeModeSystemNow: Following this computer’s setting, which is currently {mode}. It changes with the desktop, including mid-show.
settings.accentColorHelp: Used for selection, playing cues and anything that wants your eye. It changes nothing about how the show sounds.
settings.sectionAboutHelp: Which version is running, who wrote it, and the licence it is under.

playlist.importHint: Use the import buttons or drag files here

properties.title: Properties
properties.peakWarning: This item's loudness is significantly above the target level for your selected output target. Use 'Auto-adjust volume' to normalise it, or change the Output Target.
properties.noSelection: Select an item to view properties
properties.busNone: No buses yet — add one in the mixer.
properties.busHelp: Which bus this cue plays through. Where that bus goes — output, level, processing — is set in the mixer.
properties.busGroupHelp: Which bus this group's cues play through. A cue inside it follows this unless it sets its own.
properties.ltcOutputTimecodeHelp: Send SMPTE Linear Timecode to the project's LTC output while this cue plays.
properties.ltcRequiresOutput: Choose an LTC output in Settings › Audio to enable timecode output.
properties.multiSelectWaveform: Multiple items selected — choose a single item to display its waveform.
properties.multiSelectOutPointDisabled: Disabled for multiple selection (out point depends on each item's duration).
properties.volumeDbInput: Type a level in dB, e.g. -6.5 (or -inf for silence)
properties.manualStopFadeHint: How long this cue fades out when you press Stop. 0 stops it instantly.
properties.loopCrossfadeHint: Blends the end of the loop into its start over this many seconds, so it fades back into itself. 0 loops without a blend.
properties.loopCrossfadeNeedsLoop: Set this cue's end behaviour to Loop to use a loop crossfade.
properties.advanceDelayHint: After this cue ends, wait this long before its end behaviour starts the next cue. Ignored while a crossfade or Start Next is set.

playback.startNextCountdown: Time until the next track starts

actions.cueToContinue: Cue to Continue: finish this loop, then advance
actions.jumpCue: Jump Cue: stop now and advance immediately
actions.previewNoBus: No Preview output yet — open the mixer and give the Preview bus an output

login.title: Sign in
login.message: The LivePlay server at {url} requires a sign-in.
login.setupMessage: This server has no accounts yet. The first one you create is an administrator, and from then on everyone needs to sign in.
login.name: User name
login.setupNote: At least {min} characters. Keep it somewhere safe — if this password is lost, the only way back in is deleting users.json on the server machine.
login.passwordsDiffer: The two passwords do not match.
login.hint: Ask whoever set this server up if you do not have an account. Nothing plays until you sign in.
login.setupHint: Until an account exists, anyone who can reach this server can run the show.

connectionLost.title: Connection lost
connectionLost.message: The connection to the LivePlay server at {url} has been lost.
connectionLost.locked: Playback and editing are paused until the connection is back — changes made now could not be sent to the server.
connectionLost.reconnectHint: Retry now contacts the same server immediately instead of waiting for the next automatic attempt.
connectionLost.restartHint: Restart relaunches just the client (the audio server keeps running).

sessionRecovery.title: Server restarted
sessionRecovery.message: The connection is back, but the server no longer has a project open — it was most likely restarted. Your project is still here on this computer.
sessionRecovery.resumeHint: Continue session reopens this project on the server so you can carry on.
sessionRecovery.startFreshHint: Start fresh closes it and returns to the welcome screen.

serverSettings.engineNotRunning: Engine not running — Apply to start it

serverConfig.title: Machine configuration
serverConfig.intro: Settings that belong to this machine rather than to the show. Stored in
serverConfig.adminOnly: Only an administrator can see or change this machine's configuration.
serverConfig.unavailable: The server's configuration could not be read.
serverConfig.locked: This machine's configuration is locked. It can only be changed at the machine itself.
serverConfig.overriddenHelp: editing here takes effect once that is removed
serverConfig.restartRequired: Saved. Restart the server to apply: {keys}.
serverConfig.savedButOverridden: Saved, but not in force — set at launch: {keys}.
serverConfig.meterRateHelp: How often this screen receives meter updates. Lower it on a tablet over Wi-Fi; it affects only this connection, not the desk, and not what the meters catch.

users.authOff: Authentication is off — anyone who can reach this server can run the show.
users.authOffHelp: That is how every release before 2.5 behaved, and it is unchanged until you create the first account. Creating one turns authentication on for every client of this server, and that account is made an administrator.
users.authOffExplicit: This server has accounts, but the login has been turned off — anyone who can reach it can run the show.
users.authOnNow: This server requires a login. Every client asks for a password before it can run the show.
users.authTurnOffHelp: The accounts are kept, so you can turn the login back on without setting anyone up again.
users.authTurnOnConfirm: Every client of this server will be asked for a password, including this one.
users.authTurnOffConfirm: Anyone who can reach this server will be able to run the show, with no password.
users.authKeepsAccounts: No account is deleted either way. Confirm with an administrator’s password.
users.authTurnedOff: The login is off. The accounts were kept.
users.authChangeFailed: The login requirement could not be changed.
users.firstIsAdmin: The first account is always an administrator.
users.authNowOn: Created {name}. This server now requires a login.
users.adminOnly: Only an administrator can see or change the account list.
users.loadFailed: The account list could not be read.
users.name: Name
users.addFailed: The account could not be created.
users.removeHelp: Their preferences are removed with the account, and any token they still hold stops working immediately.
users.removeFailed: The account could not be removed.
users.passwordRevokes: Changing a password signs that person out everywhere they are still signed in.
users.passwordChangedSelf: Password changed. You have been signed out everywhere, including here.
users.saveFailed: The change could not be saved.
users.signOutEverywhereHelp: Invalidates every token issued to you — this window, and the tablet you left at the venue.
users.signOutEverywhereConfirm: Sign out of every device, including this one?

apiTokens.title: API tokens
apiTokens.help: A credential for a machine rather than a person — Companion, a show-control cue, a script.
apiTokens.scope: A token can run the show and can open and save projects. It can never browse this machine’s files, manage accounts, or change server settings.
apiTokens.nameHelp: Name it after the thing that will hold it, so you know what you are revoking later.
apiTokens.passwordWhy: Your password is asked for because a token does not expire.
apiTokens.shownOnce: Copy it now — this is the only time it can be shown. The server keeps only a hash of it.
apiTokens.renameHelp: The name is for you. Renaming does not change the token itself.
apiTokens.revokeHelp: Whatever is using this token stops working immediately.
apiTokens.dormant: API tokens on this server: {count}. Nothing is asked for a credential while the login is off, and they work again when it is turned back on.
apiTokens.issueFailed: The token could not be issued.
apiTokens.revokeFailed: The token could not be revoked.

mixer.title: Mixer
mixer.dockToMain: Dock back into the main window
mixer.empty: All cues route to Master. Add a bus to split your mix.
mixer.panHint: Where this mono bus sits between the two lanes of its destination. Constant power, so centre is -3 dB.
mixer.balanceHint: Trims this stereo bus's two lanes against each other. Only ever attenuates, so centre is unity.
mixer.widthHint: Stereo width. 1 leaves the image alone, 0 folds it to mono, 2 doubles it. The level rises with wide material — nothing compensates for it.
mixer.widthMonoOnly: A mono bus has no stereo image to widen
mixer.bassMonoHint: Sends everything below this to the centre, leaving the rest of the image alone. Parked at the bottom of its travel it is out of circuit.
mixer.correlationHint: How mono-compatible this bus is. +1 sums perfectly, 0 is wide, below 0 means part of it cancels when summed to mono.
mixer.shapeHint: Bell or shelf. A bell lifts a band and returns to flat either side of it; a shelf lifts everything past its corner and stays there.
mixer.qHint: How wide the bell is. Higher is narrower.
mixer.slopeHint: How steeply the shelf turns. 1 is as steep as it goes without peaking at the corner.
mixer.eqHandleHint: Drag for frequency and gain, wheel for Q, shift for fine, double-click to reset.
mixer.monoCheckHint: Fold the headphones to mono to check mono compatibility. PFL a bus first — anything that cancels when summed will drop out. The house is unaffected.
mixer.busRouteUnbound: This bus's route never reaches the master, so it is silent.
mixer.outputNoneHelp: This bus has no output of its own. Whatever leaves it leaves by its aux sends.
mixer.outputNoneSilent: This bus has no output, and no send that reaches one, so it is silent.
mixer.noStrip: This bus has no engine strip
mixer.pflHint: Pre-fade listen: send this bus to the Preview bus, before its fader and mute. The main output is unaffected.
mixer.outputUnmapped: '{name}' is not in this machine's output map. If a device of that name is present it will be used; otherwise this bus is silent.
mixer.unboundTitle: Some cues have nowhere to play
mixer.unboundBody: These buses point at hardware this machine does not have, so cues on them will be silent: {buses}. Map them to an output, or point them somewhere else.
mixer.outputMissingHint: Output missing — click to remap hardware
mixer.outputMapIntro: Logical output names used by this project's buses, and the hardware device and channel each one maps to on this machine.
mixer.outputMapDeleteConfirmBody: These buses target this output and will lose their hardware mapping:
mixer.outputMapAdminOnly: Only administrators can change the hardware output map. Which sockets this machine has belongs to the machine, not to the show.
mixer.sendTapPreHelp: Taken before this bus’s fader and mute, so the send stays up when they come down. Click for post-fader.
mixer.sendTapPostHelp: Taken after this bus’s fader and mute, so the send follows them. Click for pre-fader.
mixer.filterParked: Parked at the end of its travel — out of circuit. Turn it in, or double-click to park it again.
mixer.bypassHint: Take this section out of circuit. The settings are kept, so switching it back in restores exactly what was there.
mixer.gateToggle: Switch the expander/gate in or out. Separate from the section bypass above.
mixer.compToggle: Switch the compressor/limiter in or out. Separate from the section bypass above.
mixer.setMasterHint: Make this the house bus: unassigned cues play through it and its output is the main pair.
mixer.setPreviewHint: Make this the pre-listen bus: PFL and cue previews arrive here.
mixer.roleDeleteBlocked: This bus holds the {role} role; move it to another bus first.
mixer.previewUnmapped: The Preview bus has no output on this machine, so PFL and cue pre-listen are silent. Pick a device or output for it.
mixer.previewHint: Preview is the pre-listen bus: PFL from the mixer and cue previews both arrive here. Its fader is your headphone level.
mixer.outputMapBuiltin: Built-in output; map it or leave it on the default device

remap.intro: Drag an output from the right onto one that's missing, or click one and then the other. Nothing changes until you save. This only affects this machine, not the show file.
remap.allConnected: Every output this show uses is connected.
remap.kindUnknown: Not set up on this machine
remap.pickAvailable: Now pick an output on the right
remap.pickSlot: Now pick an output on the left to send it to
remap.noDevices: No audio outputs found on this machine.
remap.advancedHint: Edit every output channel by channel

feeding.explicit: Set to this bus on the cue itself
feeding.inheritedDefault: Plays here by default: nothing on the cue or its groups picks a bus
feeding.groupSets: This group sends its cues to this bus
feeding.partial: {n} of the {total} cues in this group feed this bus

eq.analyserHint: Show the bus's live spectrum behind the curve: after the EQ, or before and after (dashed line = before)
eq.graphHint: Double-click to add a band. Drag a band to move it, scroll over it to change its width, Alt-click, right-click or Delete to remove it.
eq.empty: No EQ bands. Double-click to add one.
eq.handleHint: Drag to move · scroll for width · Alt-click or right-click to remove

mixer.miniMixerHint: Show the whole mixer in miniature under the channel view

proc.openHint: Open this channel's EQ and dynamics

migration.title: This project was created before mixer buses.
migration.body: All cues now route to the Master bus.
migration.busesFromOverrides: {count} cues were moved onto buses created from their device overrides.

group.containsLoop: Contains a looping cue, so it has no fixed end: the time shown is how long the rest lasts
